questions.prompt: A run_code call has timeoutMs of 30,000. How many sub-calls may its program make?
questions.explanation: The limit is 1,024 per minute of run time. 30,000 ms is 0.5 minutes, and 0.5 x 1,024 = 512.

questions.prompt: Why are failed sub-calls counted toward the limit?
options: So a program that keeps retrying a failing call still hits the limit
questions.explanation: The count goes up before any check. A loop of failing calls would otherwise never stop.

questions.prompt: A program asks for bash, and the approval policy denies it. What does the program get?
options: The command runs anyway, because programs skip approval
A ToolCallError for that call, which it can catch
An empty result marked as success
questions.explanation: Sub-calls pass the same pre-execute decision and approval as direct calls. A denial comes back to the program as a ToolCallError.
